guides.favoredWhen: Abuse levels 1-5 with Grasp and Ignite, and hold Wind Wall for her engage.

keyTips.text: You are stronger in levels 1-5: force trades before 6, because her all-in wins away from your tower after 6.
Hold Wind Wall for her E engage: without it you are her kill.
Punish her when she walks up without shroud ready.

tips.text: Force early trades and deny free farming: your window closes at 6.
Take Grasp procs with E and commit to pre-6 all-ins, not pokes.
After 6, fight only near your tower or with Wind Wall ready.
Respect her post-6 all-in: give ground without Wind Wall.
Close before her all-in outscales your early edge.
Take fights on your terms around Wind Wall uptime.

sources.author: Anguish333
sources.rankClaim: Master (profile badge; title claims 2000LP GrandMaster EUW and Challenger EUNE) · Akali main

guides.favoredWhen: Respect her Charm angles, play Wind Wall windows, and win through dashes, not duels.

keyTips.text: Take dash angles that do not cross her: she aims Charm where you will be, so vary every E path.
Wind Wall her Charm, then go in while it is down ({cd:157:W}).
Do not give her gank setup: track her jungler instead of overpushing blindly.

tips.text: E through minions to dodge: never dash predictably while in Charm range.
After dashing through a minion that path is closed for a while, so plan the next dash.
Bait Charm with E movement, then commit once it is down.
Play around Wind Wall uptime: engage with it up, disengage without it.
Finish by chaining dashes: she gets one Charm, so make her spend it on the wrong dash.

guides.favoredWhen: Dodge Q with E, save Wind Wall for her E, and kill her early and in the sidelane.

keyTips.text: Dodge her Q with E and trade: every missed spell is your window.
Save Wind Wall for her E stun; never waste it on poke.
Kill her early and in the sidelane; do not let her scale into teamfights.

tips.text: Start E and run her down when she wastes mana.
Force spells out of her: only her sure-thing spells threaten you.
After her mana and boots come online, play for jungle and map instead of forcing.
Track her jungler: her lane gets much harder with gank setup behind it.
Sidelane kills are your win condition; group only when ahead.

sources.author: V222
sources.rankClaim: Diamond (profile badge; title claims Challenger EUW) · Yasuo main

keyTips.text: Treat Yasuo bot as weak before level three: prioritize experience and health, accept missing early CS over repeated poke, and hold the wave near the turret while building a slow push to reach three first.
When one minion remains before level three, take W on level-up, dash in with Exhaust while the support follows, and commit only when the positioning supports the all-in.
After a successful trade or kill, shove the wave and reset: take Recurve Bow after a kill, or Cull and a Control Ward when the fight yields no kill.

tips.text: Ward the middle bot-lane brush before minions meet; when opponents zone from the first lane brush, ask the support to ward it so the pressure stays visible and the wave stays manageable.
Collect minions from range with Q while setting up the level-three window rather than trading into the stronger early enemy.

Run Lethal Tempo with Triumph, Legend: Alacrity, Cut Down, Second Wind, and Revitalize, with attack speed, adaptive force, and scaling health shards; prefer Fleet Footwork when heavy poke or control makes extended fights difficult.
When ahead, coordinate with the jungler around Dragon and other bot-side objectives; when even, first ward or track enemy jungle and mid positions before looking for the all-in.
Keep the wave near the turret when seeking a fight, then use Exhaust and dash access to close distance while holding the tornado threat as pressure.
When behind, wait for enemy mistakes or jungle and mid-lane assistance instead of forcing a fight without a setup.
Before major late-game objectives, seek a pick and establish vision with Control Wards in high-traffic areas.
Treat Wind Wall timing as the fight skill: denying projectile abilities at the right moment protects the carry or opens the pick.
Convert the level-three lane window and support-assisted pressure into a lead, then turn that lead into objective control and picks.
In late fights, read the game state to choose the role: deal damage, peel for the team's strongest player, or initiate when the team needs it.

itemization.text: Build Kraken Slayer, Berserker's Greaves, Immortal Shieldbow, Death's Dance, Infinity Edge, Guardian Angel, and Bloodthirster as the standard line; the snowball example runs Stormrazor, Berserker's Greaves, Immortal Shieldbow, The Collector, Infinity Edge, Blade of the Ruined King, Lord Dominik's Regards, and Death's Dance.
Open Doran's Bow, Doran's Blade, or Doran's Shield by lane, and keep Flash with Exhaust as the core summoners.

sources.author: VisionsOfV
sources.rankClaim: Grandmaster, 1025 LP peak (author claim); none shown

keyTips.text: Trade behind the passive shield and deny opponents free pops: avoid positions where they remove it with poke while taking no return trade.
Balance early aggression against ganks: pressuring and shoving is fine, but drawing jungle attention only helps when the play survives it.

When carrying, wait for major enemy crowd control to be spent before entering, blunting the return damage with Wind Wall; otherwise follow up the engage and start with Last Breath only when teammates can capitalize.

tips.text: Build lane priority and place control wards around Scuttle to help the jungler win the early river fight.
Track the tornado stacks and never force an all-in just after the knock-up expires, when the engage and ultimate setup are gone.
Step through minions with E before committing to the champion, building dash damage and keeping chase options open.
Skip roaming for its own sake: favor lane pressure, plates, and solo kills, diving side lanes mainly when the jungler can help.
Once the first towers fall around twelve to fifteen minutes, move to a side lane to collect gold and use the dueling strength against mages.
Without Teleport, take the side lane nearest the next objective and let the top laner with Teleport cover the opposite side.
Push the side wave toward the enemy tier-two tower, then take nearby enemy camps for experience while denying it to the other team.
Keep control wards down and clear enemy vision while pressuring the side lane, so the objective join never walks into unseen opponents.
When a fed ally carries the main damage and Yasuo is behind, peel instead: block threats with Wind Wall and knock up enemies that reach the carry.
In disruption duty, save Wind Wall for high-value projectiles or ultimates and buy time with repeated knock-ups for allied damage dealers.
When ahead, contest vision around Baron and force the fight from that control; when behind, defend the objective and deny enemy vision rather than taking an isolated fight.

itemization.text: Open Doran's Blade into melee lanes and Doran's Shield with Second Wind into ranged poke; run Lethal Tempo, Absorb Life, Legend: Alacrity, Cut Down, Second Wind, and Overgrowth.

Build Berserker's Greaves, Blade of the Ruined King, Infinity Edge, Immortal Shieldbow, Death's Dance, and Mercurial Scimitar, valuing Blade of the Ruined King first for damage and chase, Infinity Edge for damage, and Shieldbow against burst; swap Plated Steelcaps with Death's Dance or Randuin's Omen into physical damage and Mercury's Treads with Spirit Visage, Force of Nature, or Wit's End into magic damage or crowd control.

keyTips.text: Start with the wave close to the turret and let the opponent push; the long top lane gives Yasuo a safer chase if they overextend.
Avoid losing too much health to poke before level three; if the opponent is extended and the wave is set, Yasuo can look for an all-in around that spike.
Do not fight without checking the Steel Tempest tornado and passive shield timing; a trade after the tornado expires leaves Yasuo without knock-up or ultimate setup.

tips.text: Fake a leash or let the opponent hit Yasuo through the minions to help the wave move toward the turret.
If Wind Wall is not useful against the lane opponent, use it to block ranged minion attacks and help hold the freeze.
Contest only farm that does not cost most of the health bar before level three; preserve enough health to threaten the all-in window.
Play the side lane near the next objective; use Teleport from top to affect Baron or Dragon rather than arriving late.
After pushing a side wave toward the enemy tier-two tower, take nearby camps when safe to build the lead and deny experience.
Use control wards and clear enemy vision while extending into their jungle; back off when the next wave or objective is unsafe.
If Yasuo is the main carry, wait for key enemy crowd control to be used before entering and use Wind Wall to block burst.
Engage only when the team is close enough to follow; Yasuo is better as follow-up than as a blind initiator.
If even or behind while an ally is carrying, peel for that ally with Wind Wall and knock-ups instead of forcing a solo highlight play.
Against key projectiles, keep Wind Wall for the enemy ability that would otherwise decide the fight.
Build more durability when the team needs a frontline; take Randuin's Omen or Spirit Visage based on the opposing damage.

itemization.text: Take Lethal Tempo, Absorb Life, Legend: Alacrity, and Cut Down with Second Wind and Overgrowth.
Take Flash and Ignite as the usual lane spells; consider Teleport for top-lane objective pressure, Cleanse into heavy hard crowd control, or Exhaust against burst.
Max Q, then E, then W, taking Last Breath at levels six, eleven, and sixteen.
Build Berserker's Greaves, Blade of the Ruined King, Infinity Edge, Immortal Shieldbow, Death's Dance, and Mercurial Scimitar as the main path.
Swap toward armor or magic resistance when needed, listing Randuin's Omen and Thornmail against physical threats and Spirit Visage or Force of Nature against heavy ability power.
